description: A plan that describes the data and the methods of one kind of thing, such as a bank account.
One thing created from a class with `new`, with its own copy of the class's instance fields and properties.
A method named after its class, with no return type, that runs when `new` creates an object and sets it up in a valid state.
A member such as `Balance { get; private set; }` that reads like a field but lets the class control who may read and who may write it.
An instance member belongs to each object and is used through it, while a `static` member belongs to the class and is shared by the whole program.
The value of a class-type variable that refers to no object, so that using a member through it throws `NullReferenceException`.
A type that names a small, fixed set of choices, such as `OrderStatus.Paid`, each backed by a number.
A name that groups related types, brought into a file with a `using` directive so its types can be written without the prefix.
